name: Modular reciprocating engine power plants
principle: Power plants built from factory-fabricated modules: an engine, generator and auxiliaries are assembled and tested in a factory enclosure (a genset container or a multi-megawatt power block), shipped complete and bolted together on a prepared foundation, with no site welding. Wärtsilä's Modular Block takes one 34SG generating set per block, Rolls-Royce (mtu) offers factory-tested 10, 20 and 30 MW power blocks for plants of five to several hundred megawatts, and Everllence (formerly MAN Energy Solutions) modularises engine-specific systems for its 51/60 series plants.

advantages: Build time of about a year to 18 months from order, against several years for a large thermal station
Capacity added engine by engine, so output scales with demand and one engine outage costs little
Factory quality control and testing before shipment; no site welding
Fast start (about two minutes for a 34SG) suits balancing and data-centre backup duty
limitations: Per-engine ratings top out around 10-20 MW, so very large plants need many units
Single-cycle efficiency near 51% stays below a large combined cycle at over 60%
Higher maintenance intensity per MWh than turbine plant
